rv.q: I can't promise a whip-bang-shebang experience. But I can say that if you care some for poems and poets, writers and their worries, and love affairs that last a lifetime, you'll be enthralled.
For lovers of language and literature, there can be no finer theatrical offering in Chicago than Remy Bumppo’s wonderful production of DEAR ELIZABETH.
If you choose to spend an hour and a half with them, you won't regret it.
Remy Bumppo’s “Dear Elizabeth” is a superb example of historical fiction and a fitting celebration of two prolific artists.
Sarah Ruhl’s play deserves to be viewed as a dramatic script, rather than a collection of letters.
If you have limited patience for two-character plays where not a lot happens beyond talking, then this probably won’t be your show.
Still, DEAR ELIZABETH is a thought provoking piece of writing.
Ruhl is known for the depth of her work and this one fits into the mold of her past successes.

cn.t: Ruhl's epistolary play about poets Bishop and Lowell's 30-year friendship garners generally positive reviews for its intimate performances, though some critics find the correspondence-based format slow to engage until the second act.
